title: Popular camera support and RawSpeed unpacking
objective: Open the RAW files most photographers make: admit the popular cameras' default and common recording modes, refuse Nikon High Efficiency explicitly, then unpack the exact-and-faster modes with RawSpeed behind LibRaw's metadata.
context_summary: The popularity study found that the adapter refused 29 of 52 popular-camera samples, mostly catalog gaps such as Sony compressed ARW, the default on the A7 III, A7 IV, A7C II and A7R V. Nikon High Efficiency NEF (JPEG XS) decodes nowhere and LibRaw 0.22.2 silently misreads it on the Z50II and Z5II; the owner decided on 2026-09-30 to refuse it explicitly and wait for upstream. The owner also adopted RawSpeed for pixel decoding where exact: 2.5-3.7x faster on NEF, CR2, lossless RAF, ORF, PEF and DNG, about a third of popular-camera files. The adapter takes RawSpeed's uncorrected values and applies LibRaw's curve rule itself, because LibRaw's own RawSpeed hook dithers, differs on lossy NEF and silently falls back.

tasks.description: Refuse Nikon High Efficiency NEF explicitly, before unpack, for every Nikon model.
extra_context: Owner decision 2026-09-30: no High Efficiency decoder until upstream LibRaw ships one; refuse explicitly, never silently.

Today a catalogued body's HE file fails inside LibRaw unpack as RawError::Native (API kind decode), and LibRaw 0.22.2 misroutes Z50II/Z5II HE files to nikon_load_raw and returns corrupt samples with success; those two bodies are only safe because they are not catalogued.

Detection: Nikon maker-note NEF compression 13 (HE) or 14 (HE*) through the existing nef_compression reader, or the JPEG XS SOC+CAP bytes FF10 FF50 at the raw strip offset; plus a native check refusing LibRaw's nikon_he_load_raw() decoder after open.

Add a distinct RawError variant (for example UnsupportedCompression) that the core maps to unsupported-input, with a message naming Nikon High Efficiency and the remedy (record Lossless compressed RAW).
HE samples: Z9 5147, Z8 6618, Zf 6886, Z6III 7815, Z50II 7763, Z5II 7743; lossless controls Z9 5146, Z6III 7819, Zf 6885.

tasks.description: Vendor RawSpeed and pugixml at pinned revisions and build them into luxforge-raw.
extra_context: RawSpeed commit c835b05aecfacb7343f7c424abd620aa12116c3f (develop tip on 2026-09-30); vendor only the library sources, data/cameras.xml and licences. pugixml at a pinned release.
C++20 in a separate cc build from LibRaw's C++17; generic CPU; no OpenMP, zlib or libjpeg; hand-written rawspeedconfig.h and version headers; no source patches.
Embed cameras.xml in the binary; parse it once per process behind a one-time initializer into an immutable CameraMetaData. No disk or environment lookup.
This task only makes RawSpeed build, link and decode through a crate-private native entry point with a smoke test; routing belongs to later tasks.
Record provenance, SHA-256 of the vendored trees, LGPL-2.0-or-later and CC-BY-SA 3.0 notices in THIRD_PARTY.md. Never claim a licence audit is complete.
The owner's local RawSpeed CMake builds used during evaluation live outside the repository and are not dependencies.

extra_context: The mode table in the design is the scope: Sony compressed and lossless compressed ARW, Fujifilm X-T5 uncompressed and lossy, X-M5, Nikon D850 and the Z6III, Z50II and Z5II lossless modes, Canon 5D Mark IV single-frame, 90D, 5D Mark III and C-RAW on the listed bodies.

tasks.description: Classify the recording mode before unpack by splitting the native open into identify and unpack calls.
extra_context: Today lf_raw_open identifies and unpacks in one call and Rust classifies afterwards. Split it: open returns identify-time metadata (make, model, decoder name, raw size, bits, CFA, frame count, DNG version); Rust runs classify_mode; unpack takes the mode's unpacker (LibRaw only in this task).
Keep the post-unpack checks that geometry, stride and decoder are unchanged; keep cancellation through LibRaw's progress callback; no C++ pointer escapes beyond the handle's lifetime.
Verify that every field classification uses is final at identify for every catalogued decoder; if one is not, re-validate it after unpack and document which.
Unsupported modes are then refused without unpack work. The HE refusal stays ahead of both calls.

tasks.description: Add the RawSpeed unpacker capability: the catalog field, the replaceable-decoder table and the load_raw substitution.
extra_context: Catalog: optional mode field unpacker = libraw | rawspeed; the build refuses rawspeed on decoders outside the code-owned table and unknown values.

Replaceable decoders and their curve rule live in one native table keyed by LibRaw decoder name: nikon_load_raw, lossless_jpeg_load_raw, fuji_compressed_load_raw, olympus_load_raw, pentax_load_raw, lossless_dng_load_raw, packed_dng_load_raw, panasonic_load_raw, panasonicC6_load_raw, panasonicC8_load_raw. Whether LibRaw applies its curve table is decided from each LibRaw decoder's source and proven by evidence.

The subclass sets LibRaw's protected load_raw to its RawSpeed decode after open; LibRaw's unpack then runs every post-decode step. The decode borrows the encoded bytes without copying, uses uncorrectedRawValues, no crop, no bad-pixel interpolation, no DNG stage-1 opcodes, failOnUnknown, and requires a one-component u16 image of exactly raw_width x raw_height.
A RawSpeed failure is an explicit error naming RawSpeed; never a LibRaw fallback. Cancellation is checked immediately before and after decodeRaw.
Do not route any catalog mode in this task except in tests.

tasks.description: Route the qualifying catalog modes to RawSpeed and prove each one exact.
extra_context: Candidates: every catalog mode, including those TASK-003 adds, whose LibRaw decoder is in the replaceable table.

A mode is routed only when its authentic sample's routed mosaic hash equals its LibRaw-only hash in the evidence manifest, its metadata is identical, and the adapter's own release unpack measurement is at least 1.3x faster. Others stay on LibRaw with the reason recorded in modern camera support.
Keep the oracle honest: the LibRaw-only hashes come from evidence recorded before routing; never regenerate them from a routed decode.
